text.p: Phoenix Co Ltd, one of China's biggest bicycle makers, posted a loss of 93.52 million yuan in 1996 due to weak market demand and rising costs, a company statement said on Tuesday.
The 1996 loss, based on international accounting standards, compared with a net profit of 25.37 million yuan for 1995, said the statement published in the Shanghai Securites News.
"The weak market dragged down our sales," the statement said, adding that reduced tax rebates for exports and foreign exchange rate fluctuations had also had a negative impact.
The company's total bicycle sales in 1996 were 4.7 million, down from 5.38 million in 1995, it said.
China cut its tax rebate rate for exports to nine percent in 1996 from 14 percent in 1995, according to the official media.
